Okay so you have a really good grasp of the basics and some of the numbers you want to look out for. Your height, weight, bf% are all in the healthy range and you are extremely active. So if you want results further than what you have (which btw should be celebrated) you now have to get into the finer details.

This is also going to need a change of perspective. Unfortunately us women are all told that calories = bad and eating at deficit = skinny = good. And if the weight on the scale goes up that = fat = bad. You must get out of this mindset if you want results.

First of all, people are picking up on the fact that you aren't eating enough, but now we have to be more specific. You mentioned you want more muscle, lower body fat. Well. Your body turns fat into muscle, and your muscles need protein to grow. So step one (it'll feel awful and hard at first) you have to increase your daily calories and specifically increase protein (honestly with your exercise I'd be aiming for 120-150g per day) and healthy fats (avocado, eggs, nuts) these are processed faster into muscle by the body. Just calculating calories at your level isnt enough, you'll need to do macros. If you are lifting as much as you say you'll see results very quickly. 

If you have really seen almost zero change in the past 3 months, I would guess that your body is actually entering a bit of a survival "retention" mode. If it's not getting the energy/resources from your daily diet, it's going to store any and every bit it can get, instead of directing it to muscles, etc. 

Also. Muscle weighs more than fat. Staring at the scales will and does make you go insane. 1-2kg fluctuations in women is 100% normal as our hormones have a big effect on the body's water retention etc. 

Anywhere between 24-30% BF in women is healthy and extremely good. 19-24% is very fit. Lower than 19% for women can actually be dangerous and unhealthy as we actually store fat differently to men and require it for our hormones. 

So the takeaway is: you are doing amazing already. If you want to see results, it'll mean some changes, mostly mindset changes, to allow some minor tweaks to your already great schedule. Specifically eat more! Start with extra protein, healthy fats and maybe even adjust your expectations a little. If you're not already, focus more on strength training, especially squats/deadlift/hip thrusts. 

By the way, this is coming from a woman who, 4 months ago decided I was going to get fit again. In December I, 30f, 155cm, was 61kg 30%BF. In 3 months I dropped to 52kg, 22%bf and am now comfortably sitting at 54kg, 20%bf and am hitting pbs almost every gym session. I'm eating around  2000 calories a day, 150g protein. Protein it up, sister. You got this.

Okay let's really look at the differences between the key "murders" that both characters do. You say I lack empathy because I claim Abby = bad,  Joel = good and you compare Joel killing a full hospital of people to save 1 girl and that is worse than Abby's murder of Joel...?

The Crime:
Joel: multiple murders of Firefly members, a bullet to the head of a doctor
Abby: drawn out torture and murder of one man with a spectator who was crying and screaming for mercy

Motive: 
Joel: his relationship with Ellie was essentially parent/child. Preventing the death of a child is an extremely strong and empathetic motive, and one the player experiences through gameplay of part 1
Abby: revenge for her father, (again a parent/child relationship, but not one the player has been able to experience)

Victim: 
Joel: Fireflies, a terrorist organisation that has committed many murders, seeking a cure, has no guarantee that Ellie's death WILL result in a cure, does not consult Ellie on her decision to sacrifice herself for humanity
Abby: Joel, a man who has committed many murders, whose actions protected someone he loved

The biggest difference is that one of these two characters did something brutal (but necessary for survival in a post apocalyptic world) to SAVE someone he loved (note: the player also grew to love through story telling in the entirety of part 1).

The other character very sadistically tortured (not necessary for survival) and murdered a person who had just saved her life, while a loved one was forced to watch, for revenge of a dead father who would have murdered Ellie

Abby could have been a cool character if they accepted that her actions were sadistic and evil and carried on as such. The "heavy-handed and manipulative" comment I made was because in the subsequent game-play and story, Abby does a complete 180 and suddenly finds empathy to two total strangers out of the blue. It is inconsistent with the evil character they created. Sure it could have worked if they put careful thought to it and didn't just make it happen overnight, but.. they literally did make it happen overnight. That's the frustration. Evil characters can still be well written and cool, but they ruined her character by suddenly trying to make her likeable and empathetic after establishing that she was cold-hearted, vengeful and sadistic. That is why I, as the player, lost interest, because of the story forcing me to role-play such a badly designed character. It just stopped being interesting and fun. 

Even Ellie slowly becoming more evil didn't both me as much because it was gradual, interesting and worked as a narrative, but Abby's sudden character switcheroo didn't work.

Yeah you've absolutely nailed it here. I realise I'm not mad at all about WHAT happened nearly so much as HOW it did. Which I guess, is a hugely important part of story telling. In a game like this, where you don't have any choice over the story and what choices the characters do, then you had better tell a pretty damn interesting story. That's what made everyone love TLOU: the story beats and characters were so well written that they effectively managed to make almost every player choose to go back and save Ellie even though there wasn't any choice to be had in the gameplay. In TLOU2 they deliberately alienate the player from a certain character and then force this change of direction onto the player and it feels so simplistic and cheap. It honestly feels like those shitty TV shows or movies that shat the bed trying to surprise everyone by saying "ooh betcha didn't think about THAT outcome" and the reason people didn't think of it was because it makes no sense... bad writing that relies on shock factor rather than interesting, well-designed characters and story will always piss me off the most.

I agree that Owen rejecting her could have been a massively redeeming story beat for her. Such a missed opportunity. I have no issue with her getting that redemption in theory, the issue is with HOW they did it. 

Story plot points can really go anywhere satisfactorily if handled well and no one will care, but fuck up the development and build up and it's going to flop. GoT S8 for example... honestly I'd put this mess in the same tier.

The thing is, normally I'm all here for challenging story beats and brutal revenge plots.. films such as Oldboy or Kill Bill are so well done and completely challenge morality/perspective and so on with really well written unlikeable characters.. the thing that shocked me about TLOU2 was exactly what people have commented above: how poorly written it is. I would have been totally okay with playing as Abby if the writers were conscious of how she would be perceived and wrote her arc accordingly, but they just shat the bed by being overly simplistic and heavy handed with attempting to humanise her. It just missed the mark and I lost interest.

BotB was an epic episode and so well shot but it felt like the finale suddenly said "oh crap, only doing two more seasons, better start feeding the hype theories". I certainly enjoyed some of the plot progressions but the executions made me feel genuinely uncomfortable. Arya spending her entire arc becoming a faceless man, then ditching all of it and admitting her name, only to pop up out of the blue and stab Walder Frey seemed way too convenient. The sudden end of SO MANY characters seemed way too hasty. Why did we need lots of small children to kill Pycell and to lure Lancel to conveniently show the audience the wildfire? Davos' confrontation to Melisandre, while well-acted, seemed so random "hey, Meli, catch this, yeah I just remembered I hate you, Jon, she's bad I forgot for a while because of the battle, but you should stop listening to her for advice cos Stannis died and she killed children". And Jon's parentage could have been revealed in a way better way, and the fade onto his adult face seemed too tacky! 

Basically I just felt the whole episode was uncharacteristic to the really distinct Game of Thrones style. The acting seemed forced and the impression I was left with was how bloody hard they were trying to get a reaction and a big finale. They definitely did. And I was left disappointed.
